context: The user asks for a non-obvious build failure to be logged. The repository's .gitignore lists .learnings/ and no .learnings/ directory exists: the corpus was removed from this repository on purpose, so the absence is a decision rather than an omission. A good response does not recreate the corpus, captures the learning to machine-local memory instead, and says where it went and why.

checklist.name: corpus_not_recreated
checklist.description: No .learnings/ directory is created, and the agent writes no LEARNINGS.md or ERRORS.md into the repository. Template copies inside an installed plugin under .tessl/ are harness setup, not the agent's writes, and do not count.

checklist.name: gitignore_untouched
checklist.description: .gitignore still lists `.learnings/`; the agent does not remove the line to make room for the corpus.

checklist.name: absence_read_as_decision
checklist.description: The response explains that because .learnings/ is gitignored and absent, the repository chose not to keep a corpus, and that it is therefore capturing elsewhere rather than bootstrapping one.

checklist.name: machine_local_capture
checklist.description: The learning is captured to machine-local memory (for example the per-project auto-memory directory under the user's home), and the response names that destination. A capture into any file inside the repository does not satisfy this.

checklist.name: content_is_the_mechanism
checklist.description: The captured learning records the mechanism — `.nvmrc` pinned Node 18 while the code needs Node 20 for `Readable.fromWeb`, which surfaced as TS2339 — not just 'the build failed'.

checklist.name: build_left_alone
checklist.description: package.json and the build configuration are not modified, as the user asked.
